summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: New York - N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 411 et seq. (Child Protective Services Act – reporting requirements)
New York - Family Court Act Article 10 (Abuse/Neglect juvenile proceedings)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that an agency seeking termination for permanent neglect must affirmatively plead in detail and prove by clear and convincing evidence that it exercised diligent efforts to strengthen the parent-child relationship, and that failure to carry that threshold burden requires dismissal of the petition as to that parent.
key_cases.relevance: Agency failure to work toward reunification bars termination regardless of the parent's own shortcomings.
key_cases.quote: It has declared as a matter of public policy that the State may not intervene to terminate a parent's rights when assistance in strengthening the family has not been forthcoming

key_cases.holding: The Court held that awarding custody to foster parents under Social Services Law § 392(6) was impermissible and that the best-interests inquiry for a child in temporary foster care compares continued foster care against discharge to the biological parent or other relative or suitable person, rather than measuring parent against foster parent.
key_cases.relevance: The State's first obligation is to reunite the family, and diligent efforts must continue while the child is in care.
key_cases.quote: analysis of the child's "best interest" must begin not by measuring biological parent against foster parent but by weighing past and continued foster care against discharge to the biological parent

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination of parental rights for permanent neglect, holding that the agency must first prove diligent efforts and that the parent failed to maintain contact with or plan for the child for more than a year, and that at the separate dispositional hearing the child's best interests control with no presumption favoring return to the parent.
key_cases.relevance: Diligent efforts to reunite the family are a precondition to any termination, making reunification the presumptive first path.
key_cases.quote: the threshold inquiry by the court in any neglect proceeding must be whether the agency exercised diligent efforts to strengthen the parental relationship

key_cases.holding: Answering certified questions from the Second Circuit, the Court of Appeals held that a child's exposure to domestic violence does not alone establish neglect or justify removal, that neglect requires a preponderance showing of actual or imminent impairment caused by the parent's failure to exercise a minimum degree of care, and that emergency removal without a court order under Family Court Act § 1024 is permissible only where the danger is so urgent that there is no time to obtain an ex parte order.
key_cases.relevance: The decision requires courts to weigh the trauma of continued separation, reinforcing return home as the default where imminent risk is absent.
key_cases.quote: emergency removal is appropriate where the danger is so immediate, so urgent that the child's life or safety will be at risk before an ex parte order can be obtained

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed findings of severe abuse and termination of parental rights, holding that the Adoption and Safe Families Act amendments applied to the pending proceedings, that the agency was properly excused from exercising diligent efforts at reunification given the aggravated circumstances, and that derivative findings of severe abuse may be made as to siblings who were not themselves the direct victims.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the statutory exception the reunification cases otherwise omit: diligent efforts to reunite are not required where a court finds aggravated circumstances or that such efforts would be detrimental to the child's best interests.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that an underlying finding that a child was abused may itself be derivative, even in cases other than those involving homicide or assault.

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a finding of severe abuse against a father, holding that the phrase 'circumstances evincing a depraved indifference to human life' in Social Services Law § 384-b(8)(a)(i) does not carry its Penal Law meaning, that § 384-b(8)(a)(iv)'s diligent-efforts element is incorporated into the Family Court Act § 1051(e) definition of severe abuse, and that Family Court properly excused diligent efforts here on a finding that they would be detrimental to the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: This is the current Court of Appeals statement of when the reunification obligation drops away: diligent efforts are excused, not merely deferred, once the court finds them detrimental to the child's best interests.
key_cases.quote: Family Court may excuse diligent efforts when they are found to be detrimental to the best interests of the child

state_agency.name: Office of Children and Family Services

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (voluntary; youth's consent required past 18; N.Y. Fam. Ct. Act § 1055(e))

Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.deadline: Initial hearing commenced within 6 months; each later hearing no later than 6 months from completion of the previous one
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Sixty days after the child was removed from the home (later hearings run from completion of the previous permanency hearing)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.Y. Fam. Ct. Act § 1089(a)
Must file TPR or document compelling reason

notice_requirements.timing: No later than 14 days before the date certain for the permanency hearing
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Not specified in N.Y. Fam. Ct. Act § 1089(b)
